title: Anticoncentration under hypercontractivity
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have positive uniform $L^2$ norm. Suppose $0<\rho<1$ and, for every $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the uniform $L^4$ norm of $x\mapsto a+\rho bX(x)$ is at most the uniform $L^2$ norm of $x\mapsto a+bX(x)$. For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $0<t<1$, the uniform probability that $|X(x)-\theta|>t\,\|X\|_2$ is at least $(1-t^2)^2\rho^4$, where $\|X\|_2$ denotes the uniform $L^2$ norm.
hypotheses_covered: The stated uniform $L^4$-to-$L^2$ contraction holds for all real $a,b$
